# Polished product films

A browser screenshot is downscaled to at most 1280 px wide by default; save a
frame for the film by resizing the tab `freeform` to the output size with `preview_resize`,
then `preview_snapshot` `save=true` with `screenshotSize: "full"`.
A `preview_recording` take is only as large as the docked preview panel; enlarging
it cannot recover detail.
For a physical product rendered in 3D, read
[product hero](../../blender/SKILL.md#physical-product-rendering-pitfalls) for its Blender pitfalls. To put a real recording
on a laptop, phone or monitor in a generated scene, read
[screen inserts](screen-inserts.md).

## Recorded scenes

Screen recording is macOS only; elsewhere use the user's own recordings.

# Real screens in generated scenes

Put a real recording on a laptop, phone or monitor inside a generated scene.

Use a generated still or clip for the surrounding scene, then composite the real
recording onto its screen; keep readable product UI out of the generated image.

## Composite: photographed, not pasted

Save the track, the compositor and the finishing settings with the project, so a
revised recording reuses them. A new camera move needs a new track.

# Quick walkthroughs and tutorials

Browser automation can obtain clean
states, element bounds, screenshots, or short recordings; use the supported browser
tools rather than starting another automation stack. A preview recording is panel-sized;
for full-frame shots resize the tab to the output size, then `preview_snapshot`
`screenshotSize: "full"`; or, on Windows and
Linux, where Voyager can't record the screen, the user's own recordings. Native integrations can set
up desktop apps; use visible pointer control only when it helps the demonstration.

---
name: make-product-demo
description: "Make software demo videos, tutorials, app promos, launch videos or interactive product walkthroughs from actual UI, screenshots or recordings."
applications:
  - id: browser
    role: primary
  - id: remotion
    role: alternative
  - id: hyperframes
    role: alternative
  - id: resolve
    role: alternative
  - id: ffmpeg
    role: fallback
voyager:
  schemaVersion: 1
  design: optional
---

Record only when useful.

For composed promos, bring the [motion-designer mindset](../make-motion-graphics/SKILL.md#design-like-a-motion-designer): let real UI be the hero, move into what matters, vary framing and keep copy short enough to leave the product room.

Screen recording is macOS only; computer control also works on Windows (not Linux). For browser frames, first `preview_resize` the tab `freeform` to the
output size, then `preview_snapshot` `save=true` with `screenshotSize: "full"`.

- [Quick walkthroughs and tutorials](references/walkthroughs.md): light production,
  live or separate narration, and interactive alternatives when appropriate.
- Generated narration: [voiceover](../voiceover/SKILL.md). Check `voyager voice agent capabilities`
  `narration` before scripting it; when narration is unavailable, make a captions-led cut.
- [Polished product films](references/product-films.md): authentic product states,
  clear transformation, composed motion, and targeted revisions.
- [Screen inserts](references/screen-inserts.md): a real recording on a device in a
  generated scene, with a moving camera and a photographed-looking composite.
- If recording: [recorded demos](../computer-use/references/recorded-demos.md) and
  [screen-capture](../screen-capture/SKILL.md).
- If their own footage has someone talking, [edit by text](../edit-video/SKILL.md) is available.
- For assembly, choose available [editing routes](../screen-capture/references/editing-routes.md),
  or [motion graphics](../make-motion-graphics/SKILL.md).
- Export review: [review](../make-ai-video/SKILL.md#generate-check-deliver).

## Keep the interface readable

Screens come from the product: the user's screenshots and recordings, a
capture you make, or the interface rebuilt in code from them
([product UI](../make-motion-graphics/references/product-ui.md)). Move them with
deterministic motion (pans, zooms, crops, masks, highlights, cursor paths) and set every headline, label and callout as real type. Never pass a
screenshot to an image-to-video, reference-to-video or text-to-video model, or ask
a model to draw the interface when it must match the product: repeated generation
has produced garbled labels rather than exact UI text. Generated clips are for
shots without product UI (an incidental screen stays off or unreadable). If the
user explicitly asks a model to animate or draw their interface, say once that its
text may not be exact, then generate those shots; the check below then covers only
the real screens. Without screenshots or access, ask for them before building.
Before delivering, unless the user said not to review, sample the export at
each moment UI text is on screen and compare against the source screens: labels
must read and match. Fix scale, crop, motion
blur or compression (a higher bitrate, a slower move, a tighter crop) and
re-export. If the source cannot support readable text at delivery size, explain
the limitation and available crops or source replacements.

## Source resolution

A source shown full-frame or pushed in must have enough pixels for the output
size and crop. A `preview_recording` take is the docked panel's on-screen size;
it does not gain detail when enlarged. For full-resolution browser stills, use
`preview_resize` and `preview_snapshot` as described above.
For brand continuity, use the supplied brand artwork and product references.

## Inspect screens and motion

Stills can expose unreadable UI, missing fonts and incorrect product states;
they cannot reveal jitter or transition glitches. Render and open a motion range
when diagnosing those problems. [Remotion](../remotion/SKILL.md#check-stills-and-a-short-range)
has still and frame-range render commands; other editors can export equivalent samples.
Choose samples appropriate to the cut and inspect text at delivery size against
the source. Available fonts are not necessarily installed in the renderer; check
the actual rendered type. Remotion's [smooth motion](../remotion/SKILL.md#smooth-motion)
reference covers live-text micro-jitter during slow zooms.
`voyager files present PATH --deliverable none --json` can show inspection output
in the Files pane without marking it as the deliverable. Use a one-line progress
note without an inline markdown embed; the Files pane already shows a card.
Continue building the cut without waiting for an answer: this is your own
inspection, not an approval request.

For continuous motion, sync or how a clip sounds, use [watch and listen](../make-ai-video/references/understanding.md) (paid upload).
